newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Profit takers hit European stocks, dlr firm.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Profit takers hit European stocks, dlr firm.

text.p: Profit takers halted the bull run on most European stock markets on Thursday despite a storming close on Wall Street, with London blue chips failing to break the 5,000 barrier by only seven points.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar was firm in the mid 1.79 mark range and above 116 yen after a smaller than expected rise in the Japanese trade surplus. Dealers said the Italian central bank was buying marks for lire.
Before European markets opened, everyone forecast that Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average broke through 8,000 points for the first time on Wednesday, would provoke another surge.
The Dow ended up 63.17 points at 8,038.88, little more than five months after it breached 7,000 on February 13.
But the predictions of a similar performance on leading European markets, which closed at record highs on Wednesday, proved only partially true.
By midday German shares were holding on to their early gains but London and Paris had fallen back, albeit modestly.
"It's happening all over Europe now," said one Paris broker. "London has broken 5,000, Wall Street and we 3,000. There is profit taking in a relatively quiet market."
In fact London's FTSE-100 index did not break 5,000 points, although it came within a whisker of doing so during an early surge prompted by Wall Street.

The FTSE climbed to 4,993 before profit takers cashed in on the market's four percent gain so far this week. By late morning the index was at 4,953.8, 10.4 points or 0.21 percent from Wednesday's close.
"The market is up 160-odd points this week so there is bound to be some profit taking like this," one market maker said.
Pharmaceutical stocks suffered particularly, along with British Telecommunications Plc which fell two percent as prospects faded for renegotiating a deal with merger partner MCI Communications Corp.
But banking group HSBC Holdings Plc hit a record peak of 22.17 pounds before easing to 21.89, up 38 pence. HSBC is expected to report healthy earnings growth for the first half of 1997 on August 4.
Some traders believed the FTSE's uptrend would continue once the much-need profit taking was cleared away.
"If it comes down, people will just buy more," one trader said. "The market will probably come back down but it will have another go at 5,000."

U.S. stocks traded in London also edged lower on mild profit-taking. "We're looking for a slightly lower opening in New York," said one trader. "The market appears to be unstoppable but must be vulnerable to profit-taking."
In Paris, the CAC-40 index of blue chips stormed through 3,000 points at the opening for the first time. But profit takers dragged it down to 2,982.96, 5.05 points lower than the Wednesday close.

The public deficit remained a worry for French investors. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin met ministers on Thursday to discuss budget measures which will be announced on Monday along with an audit of public finances.

Wall Street and the bullish dollar against the mark also got the German market off to an enthusiastic start. "We are off like a rocket again," said a Frankfurt dealer in early trade. "There has to come a time when people ask themselves how long this frantic action can go on but it doesn't look like today's the day."
However, the DAX index of floor trade later slipped from the highs although it remained up 37.31 points or 0.89 percent at 4,238.55 at midday.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar was steady at the European midday but off early highs as vague talk of central bank buying of marks provoked nervousness.

The dollar settled into narrow ranges in the mid-1.79 marks area after touching a high above 1.80 in morning trade. Dealers said rumours that the central banks of Italy, Spain and Britain were buying marks for their domestic currencies checked the dollar's progress.
"It looks more like noise than real activity but the market is hyper-sensitive to any central bank action whether it's intervention or not," said a U.S. bank dealer.
However, dealers later reported that the Italian central bank was buying marks for lire at just under 972 lire to the mark.
The dollar stood at 1.7969 marks, down from an early high of 1.8020 and just off late Wednesday's 1.7980.
It also firmed above 116 yen overnight after news that the Japanese trade surplus rose over 934 billion yen year-on-year in June compared with a forecast rise of over one trillion yen.
However, analysts said the trend of a rising Japanese surplus would continue and was likely to keep dollar gains against the yen limited for some time.
The dollar was at 116.16 yen compared with 116.27 late on Wednesday in Europe.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was at 116.16 yen and 1.7969 marks compared with 116.27 yen and 1.7980 marks in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was 10.4 points or 0.21 percent at 4,953.8.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index of floor trade was up 37.31 points or 0.89 percent at 4,238.55.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 5.05 points at 2,982.96.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1030 GMT
Gold was at $319.40 an ounce compared with a Wednesday afternoon fixing of $319.50. Silver was down 10 cents at $4.22.
